title: The Believer (2001) - Why do people thing it's good? Honest and sincere question.

commenti.body: I found it quite boring. I’m a big Gosling fan and I seeked it out after watching most of his roles a few years back. He’s very good in it but other than his performance I didn’t find it very intriguing.
Gosling is very good in one of the earliest roles of his. His interview with a reporter in a cafe is pretty intense. Other than that, it's a competently made movie with an intriguing premise.

It's an indie movie from 2001. If that doesn't alter how you view it, then that's on you. Context is important when viewing movies from the past.

When I saw it in 2002, it was my introduction to Ryan Gosling, and I remember thinking he was going to be a movie star after watching it. In comparison to other younger actors at the time, like Leo DiCaprio or Toby Maguire, it was obvious Gosling was tapping into something else. I have moved away from that opinion, and think he's in that same boat with those other actors. He has talent, but you only see flashes of it, and maybe one or two standout roles.

I had no relation to or knowledge about the subject matter of the film, but I thought it was an interesting story nonetheless. I also think it can be a universal story, if you view it conceptually.

I always expected flaws from indie films, so I have never been bothered by the fact that they're unpolished. That's part of the appeal, actually, and it doesn't matter if it's film or music or art of any kind.

It might not have been your thing, but if you're a film student or even someone who wants to appreciate film, you should learn about the concept of art appreciation, and be able to at least understand why other people like something or think it's good.

At work and not enough time to give all my personal opinions of the film... but will say I'm pretty sure I remember the director's commentary on the film actually being worth a listen and helped me appreciate the film even more - granted, I did really like it on first viewing...

>There are parts that I like and very interesting ideas/concepts that it analyses, but to me, the dialogue and the pacing of it seems bad, there were moments where **I thought I was watching The Room**

whenever I see this criticism all I can think of is you need to watch more types of film acting. lol
Yes, that was my intention, to understand why people like it.
Thanks, I'll try to find it.
You mean it looks weird to me because I am used to a certain film/acting style that is perhaps mainstream? Maybe, thanks for the feedback.
